properties.description:
The plan-increments SKILL. The temporal axis has one of the richest tool surfaces in the product — plan_epoch, add_epoch, set_epoch_status, schedule_for, arrival_delta, forecast_readiness, add_release, release_includes, release_report, changelog_view, pin_at_epoch, precedes, gate_on, add_readiness, readiness_report, budget_report — and, until now, ZERO skill coverage. Sixteen skills, none touching planning.

WHAT THE SKILL CARRIES THAT NO AGENT GUESSES, which is the whole justification under req:conventions-ride-the-tool-not-only-the-skill: plan_epoch (has not happened) versus add_epoch (has); SCHEDULED_FOR meaning DUE AT against AT_EPOCH meaning BELONGS TO, separate on purpose because one edge carrying both would be indistinguishable to every detector; modality expected (a plan) versus required (an obligation whose miss is a computed violation, the scheduling face of a KPP); and THE DELIBERATE ABSENCE OF `achieved`, because delivery is computed by arrival_delta and never asserted — a plan recording its own success is a second source of truth able to disagree with the first.

⭐ IT ALSO NAMES A FAILURE THE OTHER SKILLS DO NOT: a delivery plan kept OUTSIDE the graph — a numbered list in a conversation, a roadmap in a README, "next up" in a commit message. Anthony, 2026-08-06, pointing at this agent's own conversational queue of proposed next work: "your queue of proposed next work should also be a reflow2 skill". That is the third instance of the shadow-list class in one session — flo2's README list of open decisions, [BL-215]'s hand-copied decisions from the hxm_program field report, and an agent's own to-do list — and the first where the agent was the one keeping it. A list in a session is worse than a stale document: it vanishes at session end, so the next agent rebuilds it and loses the ordering the user had already reasoned through.

PROVEN AGAINST A REAL STALE PLAN on the day it was written (see ver:plan-increments): reflow2's own temporal axis held 24 releases and 72 epochs, and ELEVEN SCHEDULED_FOR edges, all pointing at three retired releases. Nothing was scheduled into any of the five planned future increments. arrival_delta on the just-arrived v0.24.0 answered `items: []` and `ready_to_cut: false` — for an increment that had already shipped and deployed — because its plan lived in the node's NAME as prose and never as structure.
properties.name: The practice of planning delivery in increments is served, so a consumer does not have to reconstruct it from fifteen tool descriptions
